title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 — Section 20 (Cognizance of cases by Lok Adalat)

content.overview: Section 20 separates court reference of pending cases from Authority or Committee reference of pre-litigation matters. It prescribes hearing safeguards, settlement efforts and the steps to take when settlement fails; reference alone does not produce a settlement award.
content.glance: Pending case: section 20(1). Pre-litigation matter: section 20(2). Failed court reference: return the record and resume the case at its previous stage. Failed pre-litigation reference: advise the parties to seek a court remedy.
content.study: Section 20(1) concerns pending cases within section 19(5)(i). Referral may follow agreement of the parties, a party's application where the court is prima facie satisfied that settlement is possible, or the court's satisfaction that the matter is appropriate for Lok Adalat cognizance. The proviso requires a reasonable opportunity of hearing before referral under section 20(1)(i)(b) or (ii). Under section 20(2), the Authority or Committee organising the Lok Adalat may refer a qualifying pre-litigation matter on one party's application, after giving the other party a reasonable opportunity of hearing. Sections 20(3)-(4) require efforts towards compromise or settlement with expedition, guided by justice, equity, fair play and other legal principles. If no settlement award is made, sections 20(5) and (7) require return of a court-referred case and continuation at its pre-reference stage; section 20(6) instead requires advice to seek a court remedy for a pre-litigation matter. Read these routes with section 19(5), including its exclusion for non-compoundable offences. This account concerns Chapter VI Lok Adalats; it must not be substituted for the distinct Permanent Lok Adalat scheme. The reviewed NALSA text supports this statutory account; independent current-law, case-law and PDF legibility review remain open.

sections.heading: Operative rule
sections.body: For a pending case, identify the applicable ground in section 20(1) and the hearing proviso. For a pre-litigation matter, apply section 20(2), including the other party's opportunity of hearing. Both routes lead to settlement efforts, not an automatic award.

enhancement.definition: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 — Section 20 (Cognizance of cases by Lok Adalat)
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A qualifying reference under section 20 initiates efforts towards compromise or settlement. When settlement fails, the section returns a court-referred case to its court or directs parties in a pre-litigation matter towards a court remedy.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Chapter VI: section 19(5), section 20(1)-(7), and section 21 for the effect of a resulting award.
essentialIngredients: A case or matter within section 19(5), subject to its jurisdictional exclusion.
A court reference under section 20(1) or an Authority/Committee reference under section 20(2).
Settlement efforts under sections 20(3)-(4), followed by the appropriate failure route if no award results.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Referral and settlement are separate questions. A party application in a pending case is made to the court and engages section 20(1)(i)(b), including prima facie satisfaction about settlement prospects and the hearing proviso. A pre-litigation application is addressed to the organising Authority or Committee under section 20(2), with a hearing opportunity for the other party. Sections 20(3)-(4) direct compromise efforts, expedition and fair-play principles. Sections 20(5)-(7) then distinguish return/resumption of a court case from advice to seek a court remedy in a pre-litigation dispute.
examples: Hypothetical: one party in a pending suit seeks referral. Before using section 20(1)(i)(b), the court considers settlement prospects and gives the parties the required hearing opportunity; the application is not itself an award.
Hypothetical: a court-referred case returns without settlement. Sections 20(5) and (7) require the court to continue from the stage reached before referral.
problemApplication: First classify the matter as pending or pre-litigation; this identifies the referring institution and subsection.
Check section 19(5), the ground for referral and the applicable hearing safeguard.
If no settlement is reached, select return/resumption under sections 20(5) and (7), or advice to seek a court remedy under section 20(6).
keyTakeaways: A referral does not itself establish a compromise.
The hearing safeguards depend on the referral route.
A failed court reference resumes at the pre-reference stage; a failed pre-litigation reference follows section 20(6).
authoritativeSources: NALSA English Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 PDF, pages 12-13: sections 19(5) and 20(1)-(7).

distinctions.title: Pending-case referral versus pre-litigation referral
distinctions.right: Authority or Committee reference under section 20(2)

rows.left: A pending case follows a section 20(1) ground; the proviso requires hearing for a one-party application or court-initiated referral.
rows.right: A qualifying pre-litigation matter may follow one party's application; the other party must receive a reasonable opportunity of hearing.

rows.left: Return the record to the referring court, which resumes the case at its pre-reference stage: sections 20(5) and (7).
rows.right: Advise the parties to seek a remedy in court: section 20(6).

shortAnswer.prompt: What happens when a Lok Adalat reference does not result in settlement?
shortAnswer.answer: For a court-referred case, return the record and resume proceedings at the pre-reference stage under sections 20(5) and (7). For a section 20(2) pre-litigation matter, advise the parties to seek a court remedy under section 20(6).
shortAnswer.method: Classify the reference before identifying the consequence.

tenMark.application: Read section 19(5), then distinguish a pending case under section 20(1) from a pre-litigation matter under section 20(2).

tenMark.point: State the applicable referral and hearing conditions
tenMark.application: For a pending case, identify the agreement, party-application or court-satisfaction route; for pre-litigation matters, identify the organising Authority or Committee and the other party's hearing.
Apply sections 20(3)-(4): compromise efforts, expedition, justice, equity and fair play; do not equate referral with an agreed outcome.
Choose return/resumption of the pending case or advice to seek a court remedy, according to sections 20(5)-(7).

sixteenMark.application: Identify the section 19(5) case or matter and exclusion; keep the distinct Permanent Lok Adalat scheme outside this section-specific analysis.
Apply each relevant section 20(1) ground, settlement-prospect requirement for a party application, and the hearing proviso.
Identify the section 20(2) application, referring Authority or Committee and hearing opportunity for the other party.
Connect expedition and justice/equity/fair-play principles under sections 20(3)-(4) to the facts without asserting an adjudication power after failed settlement.
Under sections 20(5)-(7), distinguish return of the record and resumption from pre-litigation advice to seek a court remedy; reserve section 21 for an actual award.

distinctions.title: Scope of lsaa-s-20
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: lsaa-s-20 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.
